_register: Swedish software addresses the reader with informal « du » (the formal « ni » is not used, and « Ni » sounds stiff or old-fashioned); keep it plain and mostly impersonal, with « du » only where a sentence needs a subject (Du kan ångra senare); buttons, menu entries and step lists use the bare imperative/stem form (Låna ut, Spara, Skanna streckkoden); no jokes, no exclamation marks; no gender-neutral tricks (write « elev », « lärare »).
_quotes: Swedish uses the same closing mark on both sides: ”text” (U+201D at both ends), « »-style guillemets »text» are rare and not used; no space inside the marks; nested quotes use ’ ’; no space before : ; ? !; decimal comma and a no-break space as thousands separator; dates as 2026-11-02 or 2 november 2026 (months and weekdays in lower case); lower case after a colon; the arrow → stays; abbreviations such as « t.ex. » and « bl.a. » are fine in running text but not on buttons.
_plural: Two forms (one, other), but the noun has a definite suffix and a gender (en/ett): write {{count}} {{count:plural; one:elev; other:elever;}} and keep « ett exemplar / två exemplar » (neuter nouns ending in a consonant are unchanged in the plural), so each plural message lists the right form for the noun.

copy.note: One physical copy with its own barcode; plural « exemplar » (unchanged), definite « exemplaret ».

record.note: Bibliographic record, as in Libris and Swedish library systems (« bibliografisk post »); use « post » alone in labels, « katalogpost » only if « post » is ambiguous. Plural « poster ».

patron.note: Usual word in Swedish libraries and in Koha and Book-IT; plural « låntagare » (unchanged). Not « användare » (that means a software user, i.e. staff).

card.note: Short form « kort » where the context is clear; plural « lånekort ».

loan.note: The action of lending is « låna ut » (staff side); the area is « Utlåning »; plural « lån ».

return.note: The action: « Återlämning » on the menu, « lämna tillbaka » or « registrera återlämning » for the verb; « retur » is not used.

renew.note: Standard word in Swedish libraries for extending the due date (« förnya lånet »); « förlänga » is understood but not used. Keep « förnya » everywhere.

due date.note: Swedish libraries also say « förfallodag »; « återlämningsdatum » is the plainer word for readers, keep it everywhere.

overdue.note: Agrees in gender and number: « försenat lån », « försenade lån ». Not « förfallen ».

reminder.note: The printed slip asking for the return; library systems also say « återlämningspåminnelse » or « krav » for later stages, but « påminnelse » is used here.

call number.note: The shelf mark on the spine (SAB signum or Dewey class plus author letters), as in Swedish libraries; short form « signum » only where the context is clear (the library jargon uses both, « hyllsignum » is the unambiguous one).

spine band.note: The coloured band with pictogram and hyllsignum on the spine; « ryggetikett » is also used but could be mistaken for an ordinary label.

class.note: A school class (3 B); plural « klasser ».

group.note: Used for a group of teachers (« lärargrupp »).

classification.note: The sorting scheme (SAB or Dewey for non-fiction; Swedish school libraries use both, the program only says « klassifikation » and names the scheme where needed); « klassificering » is the action.

catalogue.note: Written « katalog »; « bibliotekskatalog » only where « katalog » alone is unclear.

stocktaking.note: Checking the shelves against the catalogue, the word used in Swedish libraries (« bokinventering »); there is no clash with « accession register » (« accessionskatalog »), which the program does not have.

wish list.note: Books a patron would like the library to have; Swedish libraries use « inköpsförslag » (plural « inköpsförslag »), a plain « önskelista » sounds like a private list.

census.note: Registering the låntagare with their photo; « folkräkning » (the literal translation) would be understood as a population census.

class upgrade.note: Moving every class up a year at the end of the school year; the verb is « flytta upp ».

anonymise.note: Erase the personal data for good; the word of the GDPR texts in Sweden. Past participle « anonymiserad ».

backup.note: Plural « säkerhetskopior »; the action is « säkerhetskopiera »; the English « backup » is common in speech but is not used.

colour set.note: Written « färg »; « färgpalett » for the interface palette, plural « färgpaletter ».

print list.note: A list of låntagare or exemplar to print cards or labels for; plural « utskriftslistor ».

scanner.note: The USB barcode reader that types like a keyboard; plural « streckkodsläsare »; the verb is « skanna ».

wizard.note: The first-start sequence of questions; « guide » alone is fine where the context is clear. « Installationsguide » is not used (the program is already installed).

demo data.note: The invented school the program can fill itself with; « demodata » is also usual but less plain.

administration.note: The area of the program for administrators; « Administration » on the menu.

configuration.note: Plural noun in Swedish software (« Inställningar »); the single act is « konfigurering »; « konfiguration » is not used on screen.

return desk / circulation desk.note: The desk where loans and returns are handled; the area as a whole is « Utlåning » (the menu entry), « utlåningsdisken » (definite) in text; « lånedisk » is also used but « utlåningsdisk » matches the menu word.
